# Overview

Since this is a relatively small project with relatively simple figures, I'll try just making all the figures in one notebook from hard-coded numbers, and we'll see how that goes.

# Bar charts
```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(forcats)
library(dplyr)
library(ggrepel)

source("utils.R")

# Read config.yml
cfg <- config::get()
```

## OSPO Location
```{r}
df <- data.frame(
  category = c(
    "Tech Transfer",
    "Library",
    "Administration",
    "An academic dept",
    "An RSE group",
    "A research center",
    "An AI institute",
    "An HPC center"
  ),
  value = c(8, 7, 5, 4, 3, 3, 3, 2)
)
df <- df[order(-df$value), ]
df$category <- factor(df$category, levels = unique(df$category))
```

```{r}
basic_bar_chart(df, x_var="category", y_var="value", title="OSPO Locations", ylabel="Number of OSPOs")
```

```{r}
ggsave(
  filename = file.path(cfg$figure_path, "ospo_locations.png"),
  width = 4.5,
  height = 3.2,
  units = "in",
  dpi = 300,
  bg = "#FFFFFF"
)
```

## Objectives
```{r}
df <- data.frame(
  category = c(
    "Enabling good practices",
    "Supporting existing projects",
    "Developing institutional policy",
    "Engaging with the broader ecosystem",
    "Scaling OS participation",
    "Removing blockers to OS work",
    "Building an internal OS community"
  ),
  value = c(89, 77, 74, 73, 72, 68, 67)
)
df <- reorder_factor_by_column(df, category, value, descending = FALSE)
```

```{r}
plt <- basic_bar_chart(
  df,
  x_var = "category",
  y_var = "value",
  title = "OSPO Objectives",
  ylabel = "Score",
  show_axis_title_x = TRUE,
  show_axis_title_y = FALSE,
  horizontal = TRUE,
  show_ticks_y = FALSE,
  plot_title_margin_b = 5,
  x_axis_title_margin_t = 5
)

plt + 
   # Expands y-axis by 15% on the upper end
  scale_y_continuous(
  expand = expansion(mult = c(0, .15))
  )
```

```{r}
ggsave(
  filename = file.path(cfg$figure_path, "objectives.png"),
  width = 6,
  height = 3,
  units = "in",
  dpi = 300,
  bg = "#FFFFFF"
)
```

# Scatter plot
## Activities
```{r}
df <- data.frame(
  category = c(
    "OSPO operations and strategy",
    "Community building",
    "External partnerships and tech transfer",
    "Directly supporting open source projects",
    "Educational efforts",
    "Advocacy and policy",
    "Developing and sharing best practices",
    "Supporting tools and infrastructure",
    "Funding and financial support"
  ),
  laboriousness = c(35, 31, 31, 23, 21, 14, 13, 13, 10),
  pervasiveness = c(0.879, 0.848, 0.939, 0.788, 0.939, 0.939, 0.939, 0.788, 0.758)
)
```
                 
 
By default, the data are very spread out across the plot so it's hard to take in the whole dataset. I'll zoom out to make the dataset easier to see. Here I'll adjust the amount of padding I want to add to the x and y axes.

```{r}
pad_prop <- 0.10 

# Calculate the maximums and add the padding proportion
max_x <- max(df$laboriousness) * (1 + pad_prop)
max_y <- max(df$pervasiveness) * (1 + pad_prop)
min_x <- min(df$laboriousness) * (1 - pad_prop)
min_y <- min(df$pervasiveness) * (1 -pad_prop)
```

```{r fig.width=9, fig.height=8}
final_plot <- ggplot(df, aes(x = laboriousness, y = pervasiveness)) +
  geom_point(color = "#00817f", size = 2.8) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +

  # Add activity labels
  ggrepel::geom_text_repel(
    aes(label = category),
    size = 3.2,
    box.padding = 0.5,
    point.padding = 0.5,
    segment.color = "grey50"
  ) +

  theme(
    axis.title.x = element_text(size = 11),
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 11),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 60, vjust = 0.6, size = 11),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 11),
    axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
    legend.title = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(
      hjust = 0,
      face = "bold",
      size = 14,
      margin = margin(b = 5)
    ),
    plot.margin = unit(c(0.3, 0.3, 0.3, 0.9), "cm"),
    panel.grid = element_line(linetype = "solid", color = "gray90"),
    panel.background = element_blank()
  ) +

  labs(
    title = "Pervasiveness vs. laboriousness of OSPO activities",
    x = "Laboriousness (relative hours spent)",
    y = "Pervasiveness\n(% of respondents who engage in the activity)"
  ) +
  # Pass the calculated limits into coord_cartesian
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(min_x, max_x), ylim = c(.7, 1))

  final_plot
```

```{r}
ggsave(
  filename = file.path(cfg$figure_path, "activities.png"),
  width = 7.2,
  height = 3.6,
  units = "in",
  dpi = 500,
  bg = "#FFFFFF"
)
```


# Donut chart

```{r}
df <- data.frame(
  category = c("Established", "Integrated", "Emerging"),
  value = c(13, 8, 5)
)

# Preserve category order and compute slice coordinates
df$category <- factor(df$category, levels = df$category)
df$fraction <- df$value / sum(df$value)
df$ymax <- cumsum(df$fraction)
df$ymin <- c(0, head(df$ymax, n = -1))
df$label_pos <- (df$ymax + df$ymin) / 2
df$label <- paste0(round(df$fraction * 100), "%")

# Custom hex palette for the three sections
custom_colors <- c(
  "#00817f",
  "#42F2FF",
  "#B92DA4"
)
ggplot(df, aes(ymax = ymax, ymin = ymin, xmax = 4, xmin = 3, fill = category)) +
  geom_rect(color = "#FFFFFF", linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_text(
    aes(x = 4.4, y = label_pos, label = label),
    color = "#000000",
    fontface = "bold",
    size = 4
  ) +
  coord_polar(theta = "y", clip = "off") +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(3, 5), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = custom_colors) +
  labs(
    title = "OSPO status",
    fill = NULL
  ) +
  # Custom theme built directly via theme() without pre-made presets
  theme(
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "#FFFFFF", color = NA),
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "#FFFFFF", color = NA),
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    axis.title = element_blank(),
    axis.text = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks = element_blank(),
    axis.line = element_blank(),
    plot.margin = margin(t = 5, r = 20, b = 5, l = 20),
    plot.title = element_text(
      color = "#111827",
      size = 14,
      face = "bold",
      hjust = 0.5,
      margin = margin(b = -45)
    ),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.box.spacing = unit(0, "pt"), # Removes gap between panel and legend
    legend.margin = margin(t = -55, b=2),
    legend.background = element_rect(fill = "#FFFFFF", color = NA),
    legend.key = element_rect(fill = "#FFFFFF", color = NA),
    legend.text = element_text(color = "#374151", size = 10, margin = margin(t=0))
  )

ggsave(
  filename = file.path(cfg$figure_path, "donut_chart.png"),
  width = 4,
  height = 3,
  units = "in",
  dpi = 300,
  bg = "#FFFFFF"
)
```
